data.description:
The write-time secret screen (bug e7a9) is enforced at `_seam.finalize_event`, the one
seam every writer routes through. Two callers of that seam handle a refusal in a way that
deserves its own review; neither blocks e7a9, and both were found by an adversarial review
of the e7a9 change rather than by a failure.

## 1. Sidecar emits swallow the refusal

`llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`, `llm/completion_sidecar.py`, and `llm/code_review/sidecar.py`
all wrap their `append_event` in `except Exception: logger.warning(...); return False`.
REVIEW_RESULT / COMPLETION_VERDICT payloads embed the reviewed MATERIAL (diffs, plan text),
so a test fixture or a documented detection regex inside that material can make the verdict
event unwritable — and it is then dropped with only a warning, with no override path (no CLI
flag reaches those code paths). The result is silent loss of the gate's own audit trail.

Options to weigh: exempt the sidecar event types from the screen (accepts that reviewed
material can carry a secret into the store); distinguish the screen refusal from a generic
emit failure and surface it loudly; or screen only the sidecar's own prose fields rather
than the embedded material.

Measured context: sweeping the live store's 25,125 events with the shipped patterns, exactly
one would be refused, and it is a false positive (`AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`, AWS's own published
doc example, quoted in a ticket ABOUT secret scanning). So the real-world rate is low — but
the sidecar path is exactly where "prose about credentials" concentrates.

## 2. Inbound Jira translate now fails the event loudly

`_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate._write_event_file` previously called the two
halves of `finalize_event` directly, which made it a genuine bypass: a credential pasted
into a Jira comment would have landed in the store and reproduced the original
push-protection wedge. e7a9 routes it through `finalize_event`, so it is screened now.

The consequence is that one credential-bearing Jira comment raises during translate. That is
the correct refusal, but it means untrusted external input can fail an inbound reconcile.
Worth deciding whether that event should instead be SKIPPED with a loud warning so the rest
of the sync proceeds — refusal either way, different blast radius.
data.title: Secret-screen refusals are swallowed by LLM sidecars; inbound reconcile fails loudly
